newsitem.title: USA: New York creates office to aid Holocaust survivors.
newsitem.headline: New York creates office to aid Holocaust survivors.

text.p: The New York State banking department will set up an office to help Holocaust survivors or their heirs make claims against Swiss banks, state Gov. George Pataki said on Wednesday.
The claims must focus on bank accounts believed to have been in existence between 1933 to 1945.

The office, slated to open about Aug. 1, will be responsible for assisting claimants in the preparation and processing of all their claims and ensuring they are handled in an appropriate and expeditious matter.
The Swiss Federal Banking Commission said in Switzerland on Wednesday that Swiss banks had agreed to have Holocaust-era claims resolved by an independent panel and not by the banks themselves.
The Swiss supervisory commission said banks would publish a first list of the names of dormant account holders on July 23 in order to speed up claims from Holocuast survivors or their heirs.

The commission made the announcement in a joint statement with former U.S. central bank chief Paul Volcker, who heads a joint Swiss-Jewish commission probing Swiss bank records for traces of lost Holocaust accounts.

The New York office is being created under Insurance Superintendent Neil D. Levin, chairman of the New York State Commission on the Recovery of Holocaust Victims' Assets, and will be overseen by Acting Superintendent of Banks Elizabeth McCaul.
